title: Standardize catalog metadata and docs for newly onboarded quantized models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: produce a single, opinionated metadata template and accompanying docs that cover model onboarding for quantized variants (8-bit/4-bit), ensure version pinning examples for SDK/API, and publish standard performance profiles to the catalog UI. Scope includes updating the model-card template, adding instructions for generating perf-profiles from the perf harness, and documenting runtime compatibility notes for kernel/quantization combos. Out of scope: changing runtime behavior or adding new kernel implementations; those are tracked in separate runtime epics.

docs page: 'Onboarding quantized variants' in docs site/Confluence
example SDK snippets for version pinning and variant fallback

decisions: We standardize on a single 'perf_profile_v1' JSON schema for published profiles to keep Console parsing simple.
Include 'recommended_quantization' as an advisory field (string) rather than enforced; runtime will still decide best kernel at serve time.
Do not embed raw microbenchmark results in the model-card UI; link to the perf dashboard and show summarized metrics to avoid clutter.
Version pinning snippets will use stable semantic model-version IDs (e.g., model:my-model@v2026-02-01) and a separate 'variant' parameter for quantized forms to keep rollouts independent.
tradeoffs: Keeping perf profile schema minimal reduces upfront work but requires additional dashboard lookups for deep analysis.
Advisory 'recommended_quantization' allows flexibility but may confuse users expecting strict enforcement — mitigated by clear docs and examples.
Adding lint rules increases onboarding friction for contributors but improves downstream reliability and reduces broken catalog entries.
